title: Budget: the lean path, lean but keep the Phantom and the FD …
ask: Should the swap take the lean parts path at about $3,600-5,500 (a), the lean path but keep the Phantom 340 pump and the FD alternator already ruled (b), or stay as planned at about $5,300-9,300 (c)?
why:
Camden, 2026-10-17: "we need to try to be as budget as we can ... i dont want to do half assed work but this needs to be achevable with budget including the wiring costs wich is also another 10k or more ... lets look at this and see what costs are worth now and what can be resposibly pushed to luxury"

The plan's parts list today is about $5,300-9,300 (EMU PRO and wiring not included). The lean path keeps everything the car needs to run, drive and pass its test, and pushes what only the turbo or luxury stage needs. Estimates, per item:
- Fuel pump: a Walbro 255 in a universal in-tank hanger, about $150-250, against the Phantom 340 at $450-600 (D-447). It still feeds about 300 hp, so the turbo stage keeps it. Saves about $300.
- Fuel lines: the FB's steel feed and return pipes reused (00-CAR PT176, PT177), with EFI-rated hose only at the ends: about $40-80 against $120-300.
- Alternator: the BP's own (about 70 A, in the package) now, and the upgrade with the luxury loads, against the FD 100 A at $120-250 (D-633). The engine-stage load (pump, one fan, ECU, injectors, lights) is far below the 163 A luxury figure.
- Radiator: the FB's own, flushed and pressure-tested, with hose adapters to the BP's necks, against a new aluminum one at about $230-450. The 12A rejected more heat than the BP will; a new 2-row core comes with the turbo stage.
- Fan: a universal 16 in puller, about $60-100, against $150-350.
- MAP sensor: the EMU PRO's own, if it has one (a hose to the dash), against an external MAP-400 at $80-130. The MAP-400 comes with the turbo stage; if the EMU PRO has no internal sensor, it is bought now.
- Throttle sensor: a yard Miata automatic's linear sensor, about $15-40, against the Flyin' Miata kit at $80-160.
- Driveshaft: the FB's own shaft shortened or lengthened by a shop, with a Miata slip yoke from a yard car, about $150-300, against a new one at $350-650.
- Clutch pedal and master: from a yard FB manual car, about $50-150, plus a braided line.
- Tools: the stand bought, the hoist rented when needed, a compression tester only, and the mount plates welded by a shop, about $150-300 against $250-550.

Not cut: the engine and freight, the converter and O2 sensors (the test needs them), the exhaust, the mounts, the linear throttle sensor and IAT (the ECU needs them), the thermostat and fluids.

Lean total: about $3,600-5,500.
options:
(a) The lean path as listed: about $3,600-5,500. The Phantom 340 (D-447) and the FD alternator (D-633) give way to a Walbro 255 and the BP's own alternator; the FB's radiator, driveshaft and fuel lines are reused; the external MAP sensor and a new radiator move to the turbo stage. Forecloses nothing: every pushed item has its stage.
(b) Lean, but keep the Phantom 340 and the FD alternator as already ruled: about $4,200-6,100. Everything else as in (a).
(c) Keep the plan as it is: about $5,300-9,300.
recommend: (a), unless you would rather not revisit the pump and alternator rulings - then (b)
stops: SR04's parts round and the buy rows after the freeze (BR06); the engine purchase (BR09) does not wait on it
